source.title: What is the role of dopamine in reward: hedonic impact, reward learning, or incentive salience?

confidence_rationale: This is the canonical statement of the incentive-salience theory and one of the two anchors already cited in MECH-189/MECH-329. The 6-OHDA dopamine-depletion experiments dissociate 'wanting' (mesolimbic-dopamine-mediated incentive salience attributed to reward cues) from 'liking' (opioid/hedonic-mediated affective reactions) from learning. The dissociation is the empirical foundation for MECH-189's WRITE gate (a): a salience signal -- not a calibrated hedonic value -- is what marks a benefit contact for super-ordinal storage. It is a strong source-quality paper (rat 6-OHDA lesion + taste-reactivity behavioural assay, foundational and heavily replicated) but the mapping is partial: the paper is adult rat, not developmental, and says nothing directly about persistent cue-indexed goal-anchor formation. Confidence is held at 0.72 -- weighted up for source quality and direct relevance to the salience-gating primitive, down for the absence of any developmental or memory-write content.
failure_signatures: If the write trigger keyed on a calibrated hedonic ('liking') value rather than on a dopaminergic salience signal, then super-ordinal anchors could not form before hedonic evaluation is mature -- but Berridge & Robinson show wanting is dissociable from and does not require liking, which is precisely what licenses MECH-329's claim that the first wave of anchors is approach-driven rather than preference-calibrated.

The paper offers no evidence that an incentive-salience event is ever consolidated into a persistent, context-addressed store. If salience attribution were purely transient and online (re-computed each encounter with no durable trace), MECH-189's cross-episode write/read architecture would have no biological analogue in this dataset.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Mesolimbic dopamine mediates 'wanting' (incentive salience -- the motivational magnet quality attributed to reward-related stimuli) but is not necessary for 'liking' (the hedonic impact of reward, mediated by smaller opioid/GABA hotspot systems) nor for new reward learning. The three psychological components -- liking, wanting, and learning -- are dissociable and have separable neural substrates.
mapping.ree_translation: MECH-189 WRITE gate (a) 'high salience' is operationalised as benefit_exposure * (1 + drive_weight * effective_drive). Berridge & Robinson ground this primitive: the quantity that should gate a super-ordinal write is an incentive-salience signal (a drive-modulated 'wanting' magnitude), not a hedonic/liking valuation. The salience-not-liking framing is also the biological core of MECH-329: the wanting system can attribute salience to a benefit cue -- and thereby seed a goal anchor -- before any calibrated liking exists.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The paper is adult rat 6-OHDA pharmacology. It establishes that wanting and liking are separable systems but provides NO direct evidence on (i) the developmental ordering of the two systems (MECH-329's actual temporal claim) or (ii) whether a salience event is ever written to a persistent cue-indexed store (MECH-189's actual architecture). It evidences the salience-gating primitive, not the memory-write mechanism.
mapping.source_context: Rat 6-hydroxydopamine mesolimbic lesions + neuroleptic manipulations assayed with the taste-reactivity behavioural paradigm; review synthesising the authors' incentive-sensitization programme. Species: rat. Modality: pharmacological lesion + behaviour.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality very high (foundational, heavily replicated dissociation). Mapping fidelity moderate -- it grounds the salience-gating primitive cleanly but not the persistence/cue-indexing architecture. Transfer risk moderate-high: rat-to-REE and adult-to-developmental jumps are both live, and the salience->durable-write step is an extrapolation the paper does not make.
